exam.subject: Physics
exam.title: Physics 2000

parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: Part I contains 52 questions, 1.5 points each. This file keeps only items whose stem, options and answer were clear. g = 10 m/s² where used.

source.scan: HP Scan image PDF; selected Part I MCQs typed from OCR

exam.answer_key_note: No official key in the PDF. Answers solved independently. Part II completion items and Part I items with unreadable options or missing data were skipped.

questions.stem: The two main branches of physical sciences are
explanation_steps: The physical sciences are physics and chemistry. Biology is a life science. Answer: D.

questions.stem: An airplane takes off at an angle of 45° to the horizontal. If the horizontal component of its velocity is 200 m/s, then the vertical component of its velocity and resultant speed in m/s are, respectively. (Take cos 45° = sin 45° = 0.707.)
explanation_steps: At 45°, vx = v cos 45° and vy = v sin 45°, so vy = vx = 200 m/s.
Resultant speed v = 200 / 0.707 = 282.9 m/s, matching 282.8. Answer: C.

questions.stem: If an object starting from rest is moving with acceleration of 15 cm/s², then the distance in meters traveled by it in 10 s is
explanation_steps: 15 cm/s² = 0.15 m/s². From rest, s = ½at² = ½ × 0.15 × 100 = 7.5 m. Answer: C.

questions.stem: A body moving at 40 m/s stops in 5 s. The body's deceleration in m/s² (assumed to be constant) and the distance in meters traveled by it are, respectively,
Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: In projectile motion, at the peak of the trajectory, both the vertical and horizontal components of velocity are zero.
options.B: If an object is moving in uniform circular motion, it is accelerating.
options.C: As the radius of the circular path increases, the centripetal acceleration decreases, provided that the velocity remains the same.
options.D: In the motion of the moon around the earth, the force that provides the necessary centripetal acceleration is the gravitational attraction of the earth.
options.E: In a projectile motion, the horizontal component of velocity is always constant if air resistance is neglected.

explanation_steps: At the peak, only the vertical component is zero. The horizontal component stays constant if air resistance is neglected.
B–E are correct. Answer: A.

questions.stem: One of the following statements is not correct.

options.A: A single force acting on a body can produce rotational motion.
options.B: A single force acting on a body can produce translational motion.
options.C: The moment of a force can be zero when a single force acts on a body.
options.D: The effect of a force in producing rotation depends only on the force itself.
options.E: The center of gravity of a homogeneous sphere lies at its geometric center.

explanation_steps: The turning effect also depends on the perpendicular distance from the pivot (the moment arm).
A force through the centre gives zero moment, so C is possible. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Choose the wrong statement from the following.

options.A: The area under the force-displacement curve is equal to the work done by the force.
options.B: Potential energy is a function of position.
options.C: The kinetic energy of a body depends on the frame of reference.
options.D: During elastic collisions only the total linear momentum of an isolated system remains constant.
options.E: The resultant work done on a particle is equal to the resulting change in its translational kinetic energy.

explanation_steps: In an elastic collision both momentum and kinetic energy of an isolated system stay constant.
Saying only momentum remains constant is wrong. Answer: D.

questions.stem: From the following, choose the statement which is not true.

options.A: The ratio of the load to effort is called actual mechanical advantage.
options.B: Ideal mechanical advantage is always less than actual mechanical advantage.
options.C: Actual mechanical advantage of machines can be greater than 1, or less than 1.
options.D: Simple machines have friction in their moving parts; thus the effort applied must overcome both the force of friction and the load.
options.E: The greater the frictional force in a machine, the smaller is its actual mechanical advantage.

explanation_steps: Friction makes actual mechanical advantage less than or equal to the ideal value, not greater.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is not true?

options.A: In practical applications we always get less work out of a machine than we put in.
options.B: It can be said that a machine is any device used to change the magnitude or direction of a force.
options.C: A single fixed pulley is a direction changer and not a force multiplier.
options.D: If 250 J is the useful work output of a machine for a 450 J input work, the efficiency is 1.8 or 180%.
options.E: The work output is the work done by the machine.

explanation_steps: Efficiency = useful output / input = 250/450 = 0.556, or 55.6%, not 180%.
The printed claim is the false statement. Answer: D.

questions.stem: All the following statements are true except one. Choose the one which is not true.

options.A: The SI unit of surface tension is N/m or J/m².
options.B: The phenomenon by which the surface of a liquid is elevated or depressed where it is in contact with a solid is called capillarity.
options.C: Some insects can walk on the surface of water because they are kept afloat by surface tension.
options.D: Surface tension causes suspended droplets, for example rain drops, to acquire a spherical shape.
options.E: A steel needle floats when it is entirely on the surface of water due to Archimedes' principle.

explanation_steps: A needle denser than water is supported by surface tension, not by buoyancy.
A–D are true. Answer: E.

questions.stem: The statements below are about the expansion of a liquid in a container when it is heated. Choose the statement which is not correct.

options.A: The expansion observed under such a condition is the apparent expansion of the liquid.
options.B: The true expansion of the liquid is less than the apparent expansion.
options.C: The true expansion of the liquid is greater than the apparent expansion.
options.D: Under such conditions both the liquid and the containing vessel expand.
options.E: The apparent expansion of the liquid observed is less than the real or true expansion of the liquid.

explanation_steps: The vessel also expands, so the observed (apparent) expansion is less than the true expansion.
B reverses that relation. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Most substances expand when heated and contract when cooled; but one of the following substances is an exception to this rule. Which one is it?
explanation_steps: Water contracts when warmed from 0 °C to 4 °C. The metals and mercury expand on heating. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which of the following comparisons among static friction, sliding friction and rolling friction is the most appropriate? Static friction is

options.A: less than sliding friction and sliding friction is greater than rolling friction.
options.B: greater than sliding friction and sliding friction is less than rolling friction.
options.C: greater than sliding friction and sliding friction is greater than rolling friction.
options.D: less than sliding friction and sliding friction is less than rolling friction.
options.E: greater than sliding friction and rolling friction is greater than sliding friction.

explanation_steps: For the same surfaces, limiting static friction is greater than kinetic (sliding) friction, and sliding friction is greater than rolling friction. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Choose from the following factors the one that does not increase the rate of evaporation of a liquid.

options.A: Increasing the temperature of the liquid.
options.B: Reducing the air pressure above the liquid.
options.C: Increasing the surface of the liquid.
options.D: Causing a draught so as to remove the vapor molecules before they have a chance to return to the liquid.
options.E: Increasing the air pressure above the liquid.

explanation_steps: Higher pressure above the liquid slows evaporation. A–D all increase the rate. Answer: E.

questions.stem: All the following statements are correct except one. Choose the one which is not correct.

options.A: In a simple harmonic oscillation, the amplitude A is constant.
options.B: The period T of a simple harmonic motion is dependent on the amplitude.
options.C: The energy of any simple harmonic oscillator is proportional to the square of the amplitude.
options.D: Simple harmonic motion is a motion that occurs without loss of energy.
options.E: If friction is present in an oscillatory motion, the oscillation is not simple harmonic.

explanation_steps: For SHM the period does not depend on amplitude.
Energy is proportional to A², and ideal SHM has no energy loss. Answer: B.

questions.stem: If the frequency of a simple pendulum is 0.6 Hz, then the length of the pendulum in meter is. (Take g = 10 m/s².)
The frequency in hertz of a wave whose wavelength is 2.0 m and speed 340 m/s is
explanation_steps: f = v/λ = 340/2.0 = 170 Hz. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Choose the statement which is not correct regarding charging of a body by friction.

options.A: An ebonite rod held in one's hand and rubbed vigorously with fur becomes charged.
options.B: A glass rod held in one's hand and rubbed vigorously with silk becomes charged.
options.C: A metal rod held in one's hand and rubbed vigorously with fur becomes charged.
options.D: In charging by friction, charges are transferred from one body to another.
options.E: In charging by friction, the charges on the two bodies are equal and opposite.

explanation_steps: A metal rod held in the hand is earthed through the body, so charge does not stay on it.
Insulating rods do become charged. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.

options.A: The reciprocal of the equivalent of two capacitors in series is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual capacitors.
options.B: The charges on two capacitors connected in series depend on the value of the capacitors.
options.C: The equivalent capacitance of two capacitors connected in parallel is the sum of the individual capacitances.
options.D: The potential difference on two capacitors connected in parallel is the same.
options.E: The relation between the charge Q, the potential difference across the capacitor V, and the capacitance C is Q = CV.

explanation_steps: Capacitors in series carry the same charge. The charge does not depend on which capacitor it is.
A, C, D and E are correct. Answer: B.

questions.stem: If the specific gravity of seawater is 1.03, then its density in kg/m³ is
explanation_steps: Specific gravity is density relative to water. ρ = 1.03 × 1000 = 1030 kg/m³. Answer: D.

questions.stem: When a nucleus emits an alpha-particle, which of the following does not change?

options.D: The chemical identity of the nucleus.
options.E: The total charge of the nucleus plus the emitted alpha-particle.

explanation_steps: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus, so mass number falls by 4, atomic number by 2, and neutron number by 2. The element changes.
Charge is conserved for the nucleus plus the alpha particle. Answer: E.
